input.reasoning:
Estimate derived from story points using a velocity-based hour conversion (1 point ≈ 6-7 hours of blended effort, adjusted by task type), then split across roles based on task nature (backend-heavy, frontend-heavy, QA, DevOps). Team capacity: Backend 1.5 FTE (~60h/wk), Frontend 1.0 FTE (~40h/wk), QA 0.6 FTE (~24h/wk), DevOps 0.4 FTE (~16h/wk). Total backlog is 81 points. Given team size, this represents roughly 10-12 weeks of delivery. No historical actuals exist, so estimate is based on point-to-hour heuristics and task decomposition by discipline, cross-checked against available capacity per role to ensure hours are proportionate (especially QA and DevOps, which are thin and become bottlenecks/risks).

Breakdown by task (approx hours):
- PW-1 (CI/staging, 5pts, High): DevOps-led. 40h DevOps, 8h Backend support.
- PW-2 (Design system, 8pts, Medium): Frontend-led. 70h Frontend, 8h QA.
- PW-3 (Registration/login, 8pts, Urgent): Backend+Frontend. 45h Backend, 30h Frontend, 16h QA.
- PW-4 (RBAC, 13pts, High): Backend-heavy with UI. 70h Backend, 30h Frontend, 20h QA.
- PW-5 (Dashboard, 8pts, High): Frontend-led w/ backend API. 25h Backend, 45h Frontend, 12h QA.
- PW-6 (Invoice list/detail, 5pts, Medium): 25h Backend, 30h Frontend, 10h QA.
- PW-7 (Payment integration, 13pts, Urgent): Backend-heavy, critical. 90h Backend, 15h Frontend, 24h QA, 8h DevOps (webhook infra).
- PW-8 (Legacy migration, 21pts, High): Backend+DevOps heavy, high risk. 130h Backend, 30h QA, 24h DevOps.

Role totals:
Backend: 8+45+70+25+25+90+130 = 393h
Frontend: 70+30+30+45+30+15 = 220h
QA: 8+16+20+12+10+24+30 = 120h
DevOps: 40+8+24 = 72h

These totals were sanity-checked against capacity: Backend 1.5 FTE over ~10 weeks = ~600h available, 393h is reasonable (65% utilization, leaving buffer for other work). Frontend 1.0 FTE ~400h avail over 10 weeks, 220h is 55%, reasonable given design system + UI work is concentrated. QA 0.6 FTE ~240h avail, 120h is 50% - QA is a likely bottleneck given breadth of testing needed across 8 tasks; flagged as risk. DevOps 0.4 FTE ~160h avail, 72h is 45%, reasonable but migration cutover work may need to be sequenced carefully given limited DevOps capacity.

Non-labour costs added for Stripe integration sandbox/PCI review, staging infra, migration tooling/licensing, and contingency.

Scenarios: P50 (realistic base estimate), P80 (adds ~20% for uncertainty in migration and integration risk areas), P90 (adds ~35% for compounding risk if migration data quality issues or Stripe reconciliation edge cases emerge).

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration setup, sandbox testing, and PCI-related review
Staging/CI infrastructure (cloud hosting, pipeline tooling) for project duration
Legacy data migration tooling/licensing and Oracle export support
Contingency buffer (~8% of labour) for scope refinement and unknowns

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project; all effort figures are derived from story points and task decomposition heuristics, not past velocity.
Story points converted to hours using a blended ~6-7 hours/point heuristic, adjusted per task based on which discipline(s) are dominant.

QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) and DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) are thinly staffed relative to the backlog's breadth; QA in particular touches all 8 tasks and may become a bottleneck — additional QA capacity or a longer timeline may be needed.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) is treated as high-risk/high-effort given volume (400k records, 2M invoice lines); actual effort could vary significantly depending on legacy schema quality.
Payment provider integration (PW-7) assumes standard Stripe APIs without custom PCI-DSS scope beyond tokenized card handling.
RBAC (PW-4) assumes a moderate permission matrix complexity, not a fully dynamic policy engine.
Estimate assumes work is sequenced sensibly (CI/staging first) and roles are not blocked waiting on each other for extended periods.
Contingency of ~8% of labour cost added to cover unknowns typical of early-stage estimates without actuals.

scenarios.name: P90 - High risk (data quality issues, compounding delays)

reductions.description: Defer PW-2 (Design system and component library, Medium priority) to a follow-up phase and use a base UI framework's default components initially
reductions.effect: Removes ~70 hours of Frontend Developer effort from this phase; design system can be built incrementally as pages are delivered.

reductions.description: Descope PW-6 (Invoice list and detail view, Medium priority) advanced filtering to a later release, shipping a simple list first
reductions.effect: Reduces PW-6 effort by roughly half (Backend ~12h, Frontend ~15h, QA ~5h saved).

reductions.description: Reduce QA scope on lower-risk tasks (PW-2, PW-5, PW-6) to smoke testing only, relying on developer self-testing, and reserve full QA cycles for Urgent items
reductions.effect: Cuts approximately 30 QA hours across Medium/High priority non-critical tasks.

reductions.description: Phase the Legacy data migration (PW-8) into two stages — migrate customer records first, defer invoice line migration by one release
reductions.effect: Defers roughly 65 hours of Backend and 12 hours of DevOps effort to a later billing period, reducing this phase's cost without dropping scope.

reductions.description: Reduce contingency buffer from 8% to 4% once CI pipeline (PW-1) is delivered and initial velocity is observed
reductions.effect: Lowers non-labour contingency line; revisit after first sprint with real data.
